introduction_raw:
The following guide outlines the procedure for replacing the spark plugs in the 2.0 and 2.3 liter Duratec engines found in 2004-2007 Focus models. Replacement for OEM spark plugs is suggested every 60,000 miles.

For spark plugs that have an adjustable gap between the electrodes, the suggested gap is 0.050". OEM Motorcraft double platinum spark plugs, which are used in this guide, come pre-gapped and cannot be altered.
introduction_rendered:

lines.text_raw: Use compressed air to clear any debris from the area around the ignition coils on top of the engine.
lines.text_rendered: Use compressed air to clear any debris from the area around the ignition coils on top of the engine.

lines.text_raw: Any particles that fall into the ignition cylinder could cause serious engine damage.
lines.text_rendered: Any particles that fall into the ignition cylinder could cause serious engine damage.

lines.text_raw: Remove the ignition coil electrical connector by first depressing the plastic tab on top of the connector.
lines.text_rendered: Remove the ignition coil electrical connector by first depressing the plastic tab on top of the connector.

lines.text_raw: Pull the connector straight away from the ignition coil to detach it.
lines.text_rendered: Pull the connector straight away from the ignition coil to detach it.

lines.text_raw: Repeat this procedure for the remaining three ignition coils.
lines.text_rendered: Repeat this procedure for the remaining three ignition coils.

lines.text_raw: Use an 8 mm deep socket to loosen the four ignition coil mounting bolts.
lines.text_rendered: Use an 8 mm deep socket to loosen the four ignition coil mounting bolts.

lines.text_raw: Once the bolts are loose, they can be removed by hand.
lines.text_rendered: Once the bolts are loose, they can be removed by hand.

lines.text_raw: Twist the ignition coil and spark plug boot while lifting it straight up to remove it from the engine.
lines.text_rendered: Twist the ignition coil and spark plug boot while lifting it straight up to remove it from the engine.

lines.text_raw: Avoid rocking the coil and boot side-to-side, since this could break the existing spark plug.
lines.text_rendered: Avoid rocking the coil and boot side-to-side, since this could break the existing spark plug.

lines.text_raw: The procedure to remove the ignition coil and spark plug boot is the same for each spark plug. However, to reduce the chance of dirt entering the engine, only remove one at a time.
lines.text_rendered: The procedure to remove the ignition coil and spark plug boot is the same for each spark plug. However, to reduce the chance of dirt entering the engine, only remove one at a time.

lines.text_raw: Use a ratcheting socket wrench with an extender and a 5/8" spark plug socket to remove the existing spark plug from the cylinder head. Make sure that the spark plug is completely seated in the rubber end of the socket before loosening it.
lines.text_rendered: Use a ratcheting socket wrench with an extender and a 5/8" spark plug socket to remove the existing spark plug from the cylinder head. Make sure that the spark plug is completely seated in the rubber end of the socket before loosening it.

lines.text_raw: Spark plug sockets have rubber in the end of them to grip the spark plug and are made long enough to keep from snapping the spark plug. There are other common methods for removing spark plugs that involve using a long piece of rubber tubing to pull them out, but using a spark plug socket is the correct procedure.
lines.text_rendered: Spark plug sockets have rubber in the end of them to grip the spark plug and are made long enough to keep from snapping the spark plug. There are other common methods for removing spark plugs that involve using a long piece of rubber tubing to pull them out, but using a spark plug socket is the correct procedure.

lines.text_raw: Apply dielectric grease to the ribbed portion of the insulator.
lines.text_rendered: Apply dielectric grease to the ribbed portion of the insulator.

lines.text_raw: Gently place the spark plug boot over the ribs and twist the two pieces back and forth to even out the layer of dielectric grease.
lines.text_rendered: Gently place the spark plug boot over the ribs and twist the two pieces back and forth to even out the layer of dielectric grease.

comments.title: 2005-2007 Ford Focus Spark Plugs Replacement
comments.text_raw: Newer spark plugs are of higher quality and don’t require (my latest Bosch actually specifically said not to put any) dielectric grease.
comments.text_rendered: Newer spark plugs are of higher quality and don’t require (my latest Bosch actually specifically said not to put any) dielectric grease.

lines.text_raw: Place the new spark plug firmly in the spark plug socket so that the threaded end sticks out.
lines.text_rendered: Place the new spark plug firmly in the spark plug socket so that the threaded end sticks out.

lines.text_raw: Apply an even layer of anti-seize compound to the threads of the spark plug.
lines.text_rendered: Apply an even layer of anti-seize compound to the threads of the spark plug.

lines.text_raw: Be careful not to get any of the anti-seize compound on the spark plug's electrode.
lines.text_rendered: Be careful not to get any of the anti-seize compound on the spark plug's electrode.

comments.title: 2005-2007 Ford Focus Spark Plugs Replacement
comments.text_raw: Again newer spark plugs might not need the anti-seize compound - check with the specific plugs that you are using.
comments.text_rendered: Again newer spark plugs might not need the anti-seize compound - check with the specific plugs that you are using.

comments.title: 2005-2007 Ford Focus Spark Plugs Replacement
comments.text_raw: Regardless of the plug type (Double platinum or Iridium) In the aluminum head Duratec 2.0 motors Ford recommends nickel based anti seize compound rated for 2400 degrees F on the threads. Copper or aluminum based anti seize is not to be used. Only apply a small amount to threads. Also, a blow wand long enough to reach inside the plug hole in the head and compressed air should be used before the new plug is screwed in to remove any rust from old plugs that may have fallen in during removal. Tighten new plugs with a torque wrench to 106 in/lbs or about 8 foot/lbs. Do not overnighten.
comments.text_rendered: Regardless of the plug type (Double platinum or Iridium) In the aluminum head Duratec 2.0 motors Ford recommends nickel based anti seize compound rated for 2400 degrees F on the threads. Copper or aluminum based anti seize is not to be used. Only apply a small amount to threads. Also, a blow wand long enough to reach inside the plug hole in the head and compressed air should be used before the new plug is screwed in to remove any rust from old plugs that may have fallen in during removal. Tighten new plugs with a torque wrench to 106 in/lbs or about 8 foot/lbs. Do not overnighten.

lines.text_raw: Place the new spark plug into the cylinder head and tighten it by hand as much as you can.
lines.text_rendered: Place the new spark plug into the cylinder head and tighten it by hand as much as you can.

lines.text_raw: Tighten the spark plugs to 11 ft-lbs with a torque wrench.
lines.text_rendered: Tighten the spark plugs to 11 ft-lbs with a torque wrench.

comments.text_raw: 106 Inch pounds or about 8 foit/lbs is the Ford torque spec. 11 ft lbs is incorrect
comments.text_rendered: 106 Inch pounds or about 8 foit/lbs is the Ford torque spec. 11 ft lbs is incorrect

lines.text_raw: Place the ignition coil and dust boot back over the spark plug by pushing down and twisting it into place.
lines.text_rendered: Place the ignition coil and dust boot back over the spark plug by pushing down and twisting it into place.

lines.text_raw: Reconnect the ignition coil electrical connector by snapping it back into place.
lines.text_rendered: Reconnect the ignition coil electrical connector by snapping it back into place.

lines.text_raw: After installing your new spark plugs, compare the old ones to a [http://www.bikebandit.com/assets/digital_assets/How-to-Read-a-Spark-Plug.gif|spark plug wear chart] to determine if there are any issues with the way your engine is running. A similar chart can be found in the back of all Haynes repair manuals.

replies.title: 2005-2007 Ford Focus Spark Plugs Replacement
replies.text_raw: I found out that standard-issue air filters for the ‘05-’07 Focus are lifetime 150k-mile filters, and shouldn’t need regular replacement. My parents’ Aerostar also had such a filter, so it may be a regular design feature in Ford vehicles. There’s a little gauge next to the filter housing: if the yellow line is still in the green, then there’s adequate airflow. If it’s in the red region, there’s a problem. I do not know if the car engine has to be on or not, but best check it in both states to be sure.
